Is the financial machine starting to crack?

I’ve already written about Saylor’s experiment — how he’s building a financial structure around Bitcoin while taking on more and more obligations.

This week, the story took a new turn.

One of the largest firms specializing in investor class actions, Rosen Law Firm, has launched an investigation into Strategy. Five instruments are immediately under scrutiny: MSTR, STRC, STRF, STRK, and STRD.

The suspicion is that the company may have been spreading misleading information about its business.

A rough patch has begun:
1️⃣ First, STRC dropped below $76 with a $100 par value.
2️⃣ Then CryptoQuant analysts said Strategy should pause its Bitcoin purchases.
3️⃣ Now, the lawyers have stepped in too.

All this noise is putting pressure on Bitcoin right now. Strategy remains the largest corporate buyer of BTC, and as long as questions hang over it — the market stays on edge.

But if the company fends off the legal pressure, STRC returns to par, and the model proves resilient — this could become one of the key drivers of the next rally.

How to check which services you accessed through Apple ID and Google, and not lose access to them

From July 6, Russian websites and applications are required to remove the "Sign in with Google/Apple" buttons. The accounts themselves are not deleted, but access to them can be lost.

To prevent this from happening, you need to find the profiles created with Apple ID and Google, and add new ways to log in to them:
🍏 For Apple ID

On iPhone, iPad, or Mac, go to "Settings" → your name → "Sign in with Apple".

Here you can see all the applications and services that you accessed through Apple ID, as well as the substitute emails from the "Hide email" feature - save these addresses, you can use them to log in as well.
🔎 For Google Account

From any device and browser, go to myaccount.google.com/connections.

Here you can see all the applications and services where login was set up through Google.

Now log in to the necessary services through Apple/Google and add alternative login methods, such as by phone.

⏺ They enable arbitrage, refinancing, and liquidation strategies.

4️⃣ Exploits — Many DeFi hacks used flash loans to manipulate markets.
